issues.description: The problem statement requires calculateTotalPrice to be a static method (see problem notes lines stating it must be static), but the solution implementation declares calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (non-static). This mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about whether calculateTotalPrice should be static and will lead to inconsistent implementations or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement and the implementation consistent. Either: (A) change the problem statement to state calculateTotalPrice is an instance method (and update any notes/tests accordingly), or (B) change the solution implementation to declare calculateTotalPrice as static (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) and adjust any uses to call SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(...). Prefer option B if the intent is to use the shared static stock as described.

issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction about the stock attribute: it first describes a 'final Stock stock' initialized in the constructor (implying an instance final field), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). This conflicting guidance will confuse students on whether to implement stock as an instance final field or as a static field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement: explicitly state whether 'stock' is an instance final field or a static (class-level) field. If the stock is meant to be shared across all SealSaloon instances, update the earlier text to say 'a static final Stock stock' and remove the wording that implies an instance-only final field; if it should be per-instance, remove the later requirement that it must be static.
